To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) an elevation in nocturnal body temperature can explain the development of cooccurring symptoms and disorders including obesity, sleep impairment, night eating and sedentarism; and (ii) an elevation in core body temperature can be caused by obesity, sleep impairment and sedentary behaviour.

(a) an elevation in CBT that interfered with sleep onset can explain the development and maintenance of co-occurrances between overweight/obese, sleep impairment, night eating, sedentariness and a number of other symptoms and disorders; (b) a number of existing therapies can reduce CBT; (c) there are a number of methodological issues that need to be considered before concluding that CBT is a cause of a symptom, disorder or behaviour; and (d)

(i) elevated core body temperature (e.g. nocturnal CBT) can explain the co-occurring development of overweight/obesity and sleep impairment, and (ii) elevated core body temperate may also explain the co- occurrence of late-night eating and a sedentay lifestyle.
